answer: On an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks, so voting weight depends on trusted paths, not identity count. A sybil cluster \(S\) with few external edges has low conductance, \(\phi(S)=\mathrm{cut}(S,\bar S)/\mathrm{vol}(S)\); its sparse boundary limits trust flow from honest nodes and thus bounds its aggregate vote under the weighting rule. Calling nodes ridge, violet, or onyx does not change that bound.
